title: Washington's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: Washington's 1st Congressional District is a U.S. House district in northwestern Washington. Washington uses a top-two primary system, so all candidates appear on the same primary ballot regardless of party, and the top two vote-getters advance to the general election.
polling_note: No public polling found for this race as of 2026-04-29.

candidates.name: Suzan DelBene
candidates.summary: Suzan DelBene is the U.S. representative for Washington’s 1st Congressional District and was first sworn into the House in November 2012. Before Congress, she worked in technology and business and served as Washington state’s director of revenue.

candidates.donor_summary: OpenSecrets and FEC show DelBene’s 2025–2026 campaign committee raised about $2.74M in receipts through March 31, 2026, with $1.32M from individual contributions and $1.14M from other committees/PACs. OpenSecrets’ profile indicates her donor base is concentrated in congressional PAC and industry giving, and her committee is a long-time incumbent fundraising operation rather than a small-dollar-only campaign. Sources: https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H0WA08046/ and https://www.opensecrets.org/profiles/suzan-delbene/us_congress/summary?mpid=1052007
candidates.voting_summary: DelBene is an incumbent U.S. House member who has served since 2012. GovTrack shows she votes with the Democratic caucus on most major roll calls and has a relatively low missed-vote rate; for example, GovTrack records her as voting yea on H.R. 5378, the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act, on Dec. 11, 2023. Source: https://www.govtrack.us/congress/votes/118-2023/h708

candidates.name: Benjamin Kincaid
candidates.summary: Benjamin Kincaid is a 2026 candidate for Washington’s 1st Congressional District. His campaign website describes him as a Democrat focused on public safety, affordability, and results-oriented policymaking, and says he is challenging incumbent Suzan DelBene.

career_history.title: Author
career_history.description: Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working as an author.

candidates.donor_summary: The Federal Election Commission lists Benjamin Kincaid as a Democratic candidate for Washington’s 1st Congressional District and shows his authorized committee, Kincaid for Congress, but the candidate page says 2025–2026 financial summary data is not yet available. As a result, no reliable total-raised figure or top-donor breakdown was available from the reviewed public filings at this time.
candidates.voting_summary: Kincaid is a challenger and has not held legislative office, so there is no legislative voting record to report. His campaign website provides issue positions on homelessness, crime, healthcare, immigration, taxes, guns, antisemitism, and civil rights, which are the main public evidence of his governing approach in the materials reviewed.

Healthcare.stance: Kincaid supports a Universal Healthcare Pilot Program rather than an immediate nationwide overhaul. His campaign says the pilot should test a publicly funded model in real-world settings before any broader expansion, and it also backs stronger protections for healthcare workers.

sources.title: Healthcare Policy - Proposal for Universal Healthcare Beta Test
Kincaid for Congress - Healthcare label page

Economy.stance: Kincaid says the economy should work for workers rather than shareholders and insiders. He supports tax relief for lower- and middle-income workers, tighter rules on corporate behavior, and workforce policies that prepare workers for AI-driven disruption.

Climate/Energy.stance: Kincaid’s campaign links climate and energy policy to jobs, apprenticeships, domestic manufacturing, and infrastructure investment. It says clean-energy work should expand opportunities in solar, wind, grid work, EV charging, and transit while protecting air and water quality.

Immigration.stance: Kincaid rejects both sanctuary-style non-enforcement and mass deportation, and says immigration policy should use enforceable guest-worker rules that balance labor needs, border integrity, and fair wages. He also supports reforming H-1B to address genuine skill shortages while protecting American workers.

He says homelessness should be addressed by separating addiction, severe mental illness, and financial hardship into different responses, while prioritizing treatment, safety, and accountability.

flags.concern: The summary states DelBene was 'first sworn into the House in November 2012.' Members of Congress are typically sworn in during January, not November. She won a special election in November 2012 (filling Jay Inslee's vacancy) and was sworn in shortly after — but standard congressional swearing-in ceremonies occur in January. The cited House biography URL should be checked to confirm the exact swearing-in date, as 'November 2012' may conflate election date with swearing-in date.
flags.suggestion: Verify the exact swearing-in date against delbene.house.gov/about/full-biography.htm; if she was sworn in during the 112th Congress lame-duck period (December 2012 or later), clarify; otherwise change to 'elected in November 2012 and sworn in shortly thereafter.'

flags.concern: The 'Business executive' entry lists 'Private sector' with no specific organization or title. flags.suggestion: Add specific organization names (e.g., Microsoft, Drugstore.com) if the House biography supports them, to improve completeness.

reviews.summary: This is a well-constructed, thoroughly sourced candidate profile for WA-01 2026. Suzan DelBene's section is particularly strong: all 12 issue stances are marked high-confidence and draw from both official House pages and campaign-site policy pages, career history and education are cited to government and Congress.gov sources, and FEC/OpenSecrets donor figures are specific and linked. Benjamin Kincaid's section responsibly handles an obscure challenger — FEC registration is confirmed, low-confidence stances are flagged as 'no public position found' rather than fabricated, and the profile searches multiple campaign-site label pages before concluding. Language throughout is neutral and nonpartisan, presenting both candidates' stated positions without editorial spin. The description of Washington's top-two primary system is accurate and helpful context.

flags.concern: The FEC Candidate ID in the URL (H0WA08046) contains 'WA08', which refers to DelBene's original 2010 run in Washington's 8th District. While candidates often retain their original FEC ID for life, a human reviewer should confirm that the 2025–2026 receipts mentioned are correctly aggregated for her current WA-01 seat.
flags.suggestion: Verify if current 2026 cycle filings are listed under ID H2WA01101 or if the legacy ID H0WA08046 is being used by the committee.

flags.concern: The candidate name 'Benjamin Kincaid' is identical to a well-known fictional character (a lawyer in novels by William Bernhardt). While the research agent has provided highly specific campaign URLs and policy details that suggest a real person, the name/URL combination should be spot-checked to ensure it is not a highly sophisticated 'test' site or a hallucination inspired by fictional data.
flags.suggestion: Confirm the physical existence of this candidate or their 2026 FEC filing (H6WA01238).

flags.concern: The characterization of DelBene's committee as a 'long-time incumbent fundraising operation rather than a small-dollar-only campaign' uses slightly interpretive language. However, it is grounded in the cited data regarding PAC and industry giving.
